relevance_reason: Case report of a SADDAN patient with a confirmed FGFR3 Lys650Met mutation, with prenatal and postnatal features and a review of reported cases.

findings.statement: Zankl et al. (2008) described the prenatal and postnatal features of a patient with SADDAN. The case confirmed the severe morbidity of SADDAN and added to the reports of early mortality associated with the disorder. The authors also reviewed the clinical and radiologic characteristics of all reported cases of SADDAN.
quotes: We present prenatal and postnatal features of a patient with severe achondroplasia with developmental delay and acanthosis nigricans (SADDAN).
This case, one of only six with molecular analysis reported in the literature, confirms the severe morbidity and adds to the reports with early mortality associated with SADDAN.

findings.statement: In a patient with SADDAN, Zankl et al. (2008) confirmed the clinical diagnosis by identifying the FGFR3 Lys650Met mutation through mutation analysis. They noted this was one of only six SADDAN cases with molecular analysis reported in the literature.
quotes: Mutation analysis confirmed the clinical diagnosis by detecting the FGFR3 Lys650Met mutation.
This case, one of only six with molecular analysis reported in the literature

relevance_reason: Mouse knock-in model of the SADDAN mutation in Fgfr3 (K644M, which corresponds to human K650M); it shows a SADDAN-like phenotype in which most mice survive the perinatal period.

findings.statement: To determine whether the FGFR3 K650M mutation causes the SADDAN phenotype, Iwata et al. (2001) introduced the corresponding point mutation (K644M) into the mouse Fgfr3 gene. Heterozygous mutant mice had a phenotype similar to human SADDAN, and most survived the perinatal period. The authors suggested that the survival of SADDAN patients is indeed due to the K650M mutation. Long bone abnormalities in the SADDAN mice were milder than in the TDII mouse model, and the rib cartilage, trachea and nasal septum showed overgrowth of cartilaginous tissue.
quotes: we introduced the corresponding point mutation (K644M) into the mouse Fgfr3 gene. Heterozygous mutant mice show a phenotype similar to human SADDAN, e.g. the majority of the SADDAN mice survive the perinatal period.
This suggests that the survival of SADDAN patients is indeed attributed to the K650M mutation in FGFR3. The long bone abnormalities in SADDAN mice are milder than the TDII model.
In addition, overgrowth of the cartilaginous tissues is observed in the rib cartilage, trachea and nasal septum.

phenotypes.text: overgrowth of rib cartilage, trachea and nasal septum

findings.statement: Iwata et al. (2001) noted that FGFR3 carrying the SADDAN mutation (K650M) is more activated in vitro than FGFR3 carrying the TDII mutation (K650E), yet TDII is lethal at birth while most SADDAN patients survive. In primary chondrocyte cultures, a low concentration of FGF ligand activated MAP kinase differently in cells from wildtype and SADDAN mice.
quotes: TDII is lethal at birth, whereas most of the SADDAN patients survive the perinatal period. However, FGFR3 with the SADDAN mutation is more activated than FGFR3 with the TDII mutation in vitro.
The FGF ligand at the low concentration differentially activates Map kinase in primary chondrocyte cultures from wild-type and SADDAN mice.

relevance_reason: Detailed clinical delineation of SADDAN caused by the FGFR3 Lys650Met mutation.

findings.statement: Bellus et al. (1999) gave a detailed clinical account of the SADDAN phenotype. The FGFR3 Lys650Met mutation caused severe disturbances of endochondral bone growth that approached and overlapped those seen in thanatophoric dysplasia type I, but was most often compatible with survival into adulthood. Some patients had unusual bone deformities such as femoral bowing with reverse (posterior apex) tibial and fibular bowing and 'ram's horn' bowing of the clavicle. Surviving patients had progressive acanthosis nigricans, structural anomalies of the central nervous system, seizures, and severe developmental delay.
quotes: The FGFR3 Lys650Met mutation results in severe disturbances in endochondral bone growth that approach and overlap those observed in thanatophoric dysplasia, type I. However, this mutation is most often compatible with survival into adulthood.
Other unusual bone deformities, such as femoral bowing with reverse (i.e., posterior apex) tibial and fibular bowing and "ram's horn" bowing of the clavicle, are also seen in some patients.

In addition to skeletal dysplasia, progressive acanthosis nigricans, and central nervous system structural anomalies, seizures and severe developmental delays are observed in surviving SADDAN patients.

phenotypes.text: severe skeletal dysplasia with disturbed endochondral bone growth
ram's horn bowing of the clavicle

findings.statement: Bellus et al. (1999) noted that although the Lys650Met mutation lies in the same FGFR3 codon as the thanatophoric dysplasia type II mutation (Lys650Glu) and has a similar effect on constitutive activation of the FGFR3 tyrosine kinase, it is not associated with cloverleaf skull or craniosynostosis.
quotes: Despite its location within the same FGFR3 codon as the thanatophoric dysplasia type II mutation (Lys650Glu) and a similar effect on constitutive activation of the FGFR3 tyrosine kinase, the Lys650Met is not associated with cloverleaf skull or craniosynostosis.

findings.statement: Bellus et al. (1999) noted that they had previously identified a novel missense mutation, Lys650Met, in the tyrosine kinase domain of FGFR3 in 4 unrelated individuals with the condition they called SADDAN.
quotes: We previously discovered a novel missense mutation (Lys650Met) in the tyrosine kinase domain of the fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) gene in four unrelated individuals with a condition we called "severe achondroplasia with developmental delay and acanthosis nigricans" (SADDAN)

relevance_reason: This is the paper that first described and named SADDAN and identified its cause, the FGFR3 Lys650Met mutation.

findings.statement: Tavormina et al. (1999) described 4 unrelated individuals with a skeletal dysplasia nearly as severe as thanatophoric dysplasia type I. Three of the 4 developed extensive acanthosis nigricans starting in early childhood and had severe neurologic impairment. All of them survived past infancy without prolonged life support.
quotes: We have identified a novel fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) missense mutation in four unrelated individuals with skeletal dysplasia that approaches the severity observed in thanatophoric dysplasia type I (TD1).

However, three of the four individuals developed extensive areas of acanthosis nigricans beginning in early childhood, suffer from severe neurological impairments, and have survived past infancy without prolonged life-support measures.

findings.statement: Tavormina et al. (1999) named the phenotype caused by the FGFR3 Lys650Met mutation 'severe achondroplasia with developmental delay and acanthosis nigricans' (SADDAN). They chose a separate name because the phenotype differs significantly from those of other known FGFR3 mutations.
quotes: We refer to the phenotype caused by the Lys650Met mutation as "severe achondroplasia with developmental delay and acanthosis nigricans" (SADDAN) because it differs significantly from the phenotypes of other known FGFR3 mutations.

findings.statement: Tavormina et al. (1999) found the same FGFR3 missense mutation, A1949T (Lys650Met), in all 4 unrelated individuals with SADDAN. The change is at the nucleotide next to the thanatophoric dysplasia type II mutation (A1948G; Lys650Glu). It produces a different amino acid substitution at a highly conserved codon in the activation loop of the kinase domain.
quotes: The FGFR3 mutation (A1949T: Lys650Met) occurs at the nucleotide adjacent to the TD type II (TD2) mutation (A1948G: Lys650Glu) and results in a different amino acid substitution at a highly conserved codon in the kinase domain activation loop.

findings.statement: In transient transfection studies by Tavormina et al. (1999), the FGFR3 Lys650Met mutation caused a dramatic increase in constitutive receptor kinase activity. The activity was about 3 times higher than with the thanatophoric dysplasia type II mutation Lys650Glu.
quotes: Transient transfection studies with FGFR3 mutant constructs show that the Lys650Met mutation causes a dramatic increase in constitutive receptor kinase activity, approximately three times greater than that observed with the Lys650Glu mutation.
